headline: The dollar cracked and the vol bid vanished — silver +4.9%, gold +2.8%, VIX -11.7% — while crude kept sliding and energy equities still haven't been told.
summary: Yesterday the story was a rates shock reshuffling US equity internals. Today it's an FX and volatility story, and it's global. DXY -0.6% to 101.29, EURUSD +0.7% to 1.1273, GBPUSD +0.7% to 1.3501 (+2.0% on the month, z=0.89, turning up with acceleration 1.36), USDCHF -0.4%, USDCAD -0.4% and -2.3% on the month at z=-1.43 with acceleration -2.18. VIX collapsed 11.7% to 18.39 against a VIX3M of 21.27 — that implies a term structure near 0.86 versus the 0.979 print at z=1.72 that defined the last two weeks. SKEW is off to 150.01. The credit & vol composite improved to -31 from -35, HYG/IEF +0.5% and turning up off z=-1.64, BKLN at the 97th percentile of its year. Risk regime is unchanged at -14, but the internals under it are not the same tape.

The washed-out hard-asset complex reversed violently. Silver +4.9% to 52.00 after a -14.6% month (z=-1.65) that left it 26.1% below its 200-day at the 7th percentile. Gold +2.8% to 4051, still 10.2% below its 200-day at the 11th percentile. Platinum +2.5% off the 2.5th percentile. Gold/silver -2.0% to 77.90, finally breaking a z=2.09 extension with acceleration 1.40. Copper +1.0% to 6.4405. This is the mirror image of the deflation-in-metals trade that has run since September, and it is a weak-dollar trade, not an inflation trade — 5y breakevens are flat at 2.39, 10y breakevens 2.30 and rolling over. Critically, the miners are still marked at Tuesday's close: GDX -2.0%, GDXJ -2.1%, NEM -1.5%, with GDX/gold at z=-1.08 and GDX 14.2% below its 200-day. The metal moved; the equity has not.

What is still wrong is energy and EM. Brent -1.2% to 102.31 and -11.3% on the week; WTI -1.2% to 94.96; RBOB -2.7% and -12.0% on the month at z=-1.19. Yet XLE sits 14.3% above its 200-day at the 88th percentile with +16.9% three-month relative strength, XOP 12.5% above its 200-day, XOM +15.3% and CVX +17.4% above theirs. That gap was unfinished business yesterday and it widened again today. On EM: the dollar fell 0.6% and USDBRL still rose 0.5% to 5.4623 (+4.6% on the month, z=1.33), USDMXN +0.5% to 18.661 (z=1.02), CEW -0.5%. When a currency can't rally on a broad dollar down day, that's local stress, not dollar beta — EWZ is -16.9% on the month, 14.3% below its 200-day, BVSP at z=-2.80.

Rates remain the binding constraint and the US equity dispersion remains historic. 10-year 4.95% (+4bp), 30-year 5.32% (+4bp), 10-year real yield 2.65%, 30-year mortgage 7.24% and +21bp on the month at the 89th percentile; the rates composite is -33. The month's 33bp rally in 10s carries acceleration z=-2.29 — stretched, not trending. Meanwhile QQQ/SPY is at z=-2.72, SMH/SPY z=-2.70, MTUM -13.8% on the month at z=-2.61, high-beta/low-vol -18.5% at z=-2.92, growth/value z=-2.58, against RSP/SPY at z=+3.34 with acceleration +3.76. Asia's semi complex is the epicenter: KOSPI -18.8% on the month (z=-2.59), TAIEX -13.6% (z=-2.64), SOXX -21.0%, AMD -23.7%, MU -20.4%, ASML -16.8%. Europe is the clean side of the world — DAX +1.5% to 26248 and at the 92nd percentile, FTSE +1.6% at the 93rd, CAC +1.6%, Euro Stoxx +1.7%, Hang Seng +1.7%, Shanghai +2.2% — while the Nikkei fell 1.4% with USDJPY at 158.23. A weak yen no longer buys you Japan.

good.text: Volatility event risk cleared: VIX -11.7% to 18.39 against VIX3M at 21.27, implying the inverted term structure (0.979, z=1.72) has snapped back into contango. SKEW -1.8% to 150.01.
Dollar broke lower across G10: DXY -0.6% to 101.29, EURUSD +0.7%, GBPUSD +0.7% (+2.0% on the month, z=0.89, acceleration 1.36), USDCAD -2.3% on the month at z=-1.43.
The left-for-dead metals ripped: silver +4.9% from the 7th percentile, gold +2.8%, platinum +2.5% from the 2.5th percentile, copper +1.0%, and gold/silver -2.0% off a z=2.09 extreme.
Europe and China led global equities: Euro Stoxx +1.7%, DAX +1.5% at the 92nd percentile with +6.8% one-month relative strength, FTSE +1.6% at the 93rd, CAC +1.6%, Hang Seng +1.7%, Shanghai +2.2%.
Credit refuses to confirm the equity stress: HYG/IEF +0.5% and turning up off z=-1.64, BKLN at the 97th percentile of its 52-week range, credit & vol composite improving to -31 from -35.

Defensive and domestic cash-flow leadership is still intact and accelerating: XLV +10.7% on the month (z=2.55), LLY +23.3%, LMT +26.4% at z=3.41, XLF +6.9% with acceleration 1.84 and +9.1% relative strength.

bad.text: Crude keeps falling and energy equities haven't marked it: Brent -1.2% to 102.31 and -11.3% on the week, WTI -1.2%, gasoline -12.0% on the month, yet XLE sits 14.3% above its 200-day at the 88th percentile and XOP 12.5% above its.

EM currencies did not participate in dollar weakness — USDBRL +0.5% to 5.4623 (+4.6% on the month, z=1.33) and USDMXN +0.5% on a day DXY fell 0.6%; CEW -0.5%. Brazil is a local credit story, not a dollar story.

The rates composite is -33 and nothing improved: 10-year 4.95% (+4bp), 30-year 5.32% (+4bp), 10-year real yield 2.65%, 30-year mortgage 7.24% and +21bp on the month at the 89th percentile. The month's bond rally carries acceleration z=-2.29 — exhaustion, not trend.

The AI/semis unwind is still accelerating in Asia, not stabilizing: KOSPI -18.8% on the month at z=-2.59 with acceleration -2.44, TAIEX -13.6% at z=-2.64 and -0.8% today, Nikkei -1.4% at z=-2.38, EWT -15.5% on the month.

Factor dispersion remains at historic extremes: high-beta/low-vol -18.5% on the month at z=-2.92 with acceleration -3.28, MTUM -13.8% at z=-2.61, growth/value z=-2.58, QQQ/SPY z=-2.72 — against RSP/SPY at z=+3.34. A faster unwind, not a healing one.

The industrial/commodity-equity chain is still broken despite the metal bounce: COPX -16.5% on the month, REMX -21.3% at the 0th percentile, XME -8.5%, NLR -12.4%, CAT -26.0% on the month at z=-3.03 and 22.6% below its 200-day.

trades.name: Gold miners catch-up to the metal
trades.line: Long GDX/GDXJ — metal gapped +2.8%, miners still marked -2.0%
trades.expr: Buy GDX outright; add GDXJ for beta. Size GDXJ at half the GDX notional. Alternative: Dec/Jan GDX 80 calls.
trades.thesis: The miners are priced off Tuesday's gold at 3938. Gold printed 4051 and silver 52.00 on Wednesday. GDX/gold is at z=-1.08, GDX is 14.2% below its 200-day at the 20th percentile and GDXJ 19.5% below at the 14th — a washed-out operating-leverage asset against a metal that just reversed on a broad dollar break.
trades.trigger: Gold +2.8%, silver +4.9%, platinum +2.5% on 11/4 while GDX -2.0% and GDXJ -2.1% on the 11/3 close. Gold/silver -2.0% off a z=2.09 extension with acceleration 1.40 — the ratio blow-off that marked the metals low is unwinding. DXY -0.6% to 101.29 with acceleration z=-1.51.
trades.stop: Gold back below 3900 or GDX/gold makes a new low beneath the current 0.216. A DXY close back above 102.3 kills the thesis.
trades.target: GDX back to its 200-day, roughly +14% from 77.60; GDXJ +20%.

trades.name: Short energy equities vs long S&P
trades.line: Short XLE/XOP vs long SPY — crude -11% on the week, XLE +14% over 200d
trades.expr: Short XLE and XOP in equal notional (60/40) against a long SPY leg of the same gross. Or buy XLE Jan puts at the money.
trades.thesis: Energy equities are discounting Brent in the 110s. Brent is 102.31 and falling, gasoline cracks are collapsing. XLE at +14.3% over its 200-day with +16.9% three-month relative strength is the single widest fundamental/price gap in the digest.
trades.trigger: Brent -1.2% today and -11.3% on the week; WTI -1.2% to 94.96; RBOB -2.7% today, -10.0% on the week and -12.0% on the month at z=-1.19 with the trend rolling over. OIH already rolling over (-5.8% on the week) while XLE is only -2.2% — the services complex is cracking first, as it always does.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 110 or WTI closes above 100 on an actual supply event. Also exit if XLE/SPY breaks out to new 52-week relative highs.
trades.target: XLE back to its 200-day, roughly -12%; the pair worth 10-14 points of relative performance.

trades.name: Long sterling against the dollar
trades.line: Long GBPUSD 1.3501 — best momentum in G10, DXY accelerating lower
trades.expr: Long GBPUSD spot or Dec futures. Fund partly by shorting USDCAD if you want a pure dollar-short expression rather than a cable call.
trades.thesis: Sterling is the only G10 currency with a clean turn: +2.0% on the month, z=0.89, trend turning up with acceleration 1.36, 0.5% above its 200-day at the 60th percentile. The euro is still structurally offered (16th percentile, down trend), so cable is the cleaner long dollar-short.
trades.trigger: GBP +0.7% today and +1.5% on the week while DXY -0.6% with acceleration z=-1.51 and the dollar composite at -31. USDCAD -2.3% on the month at z=-1.43 with acceleration -2.18 confirms this is a dollar move, not a sterling idiosyncrasy. UK equities corroborate: FTSE +1.6% at the 93rd percentile.
trades.stop: 1.3350 — below that the turn failed. Or DXY back above 102.5.

trades.name: Long Europe, short Japan
trades.line: Long EWG/EWU vs short EWJ — DAX 92nd pctile, Nikkei z=-2.38
trades.expr: Long EWG and EWU (50/50) versus short EWJ, dollar-neutral notional. Futures alternative: long DAX, short Nikkei 225, FX-hedged.
trades.thesis: Europe is the only developed region where price, breadth and relative strength all point the same direction, while Japan has lost the one thing that was carrying it — a weak yen is no longer generating index gains, which means the semis/export complex inside the Nikkei is doing the damage.
trades.trigger: DAX +1.5% today, +3.9% on the month, 5.4% above its 200-day at the 92nd percentile, relative strength +6.8% vs SPX and turning up. FTSE +1.6% at the 93rd percentile. Against that: Nikkei -1.4% today and -11.1% on the month at z=-2.38 with acceleration -2.34, with USDJPY at 158.23 and going nowhere. EWJ -6.4% on the month at z=-1.63.
trades.stop: EWJ outperforms the European leg by 4% from entry, or DAX loses its 200-day (5.4% below here).

trades.name: Mean-revert the dispersion extreme
trades.line: Long QQQ vs short RSP — QQQ/SPY z=-2.72 vs RSP/SPY z=+3.34
trades.expr: Long QQQ against short RSP, equal dollar notional. Cheaper convex version: QQQ Dec call spreads financed by selling RSP upside, now that VIX is 18.39.
trades.thesis: Every dispersion gauge in the book is pinned at a multi-year extreme and the vol that caused it has just collapsed. RSP/SPY at z=+3.34 with acceleration +3.76 is the most stretched single reading in the digest; QQQ/SPY at z=-2.72 with acceleration -3.21 is the mirror. These do not persist past the volatility event that creates them.
trades.trigger: VIX -11.7% to 18.39 against VIX3M 21.27 — the forced-deleveraging engine is off. On 11/3 QQQ +0.6% and SOXX +2.5% while RSP/SPY fell 0.6%. High-beta/low-vol +2.3% and growth/value +1.4% on the same session off z=-2.92 and z=-2.58.
trades.stop: QQQ/SPY closes below 0.890 (a new low beneath the current 0.9084), or NDX breaks its 200-day — it is only 0.8% above it, so this is a tight invalidation.
trades.target: QQQ/SPY back to 0.945, roughly 4 points of pair performance.

trades.name: Long USD/BRL
trades.line: Long USDBRL 5.4623 — BRL can't rally on a 0.6% dollar drop
trades.expr: Long USDBRL via 3-month NDF or BRL futures. Equity expression for those who can't trade FX: short EWZ.
trades.thesis: Brazil is a standalone stress, and the cleanest tell is that the real weakened on a day the dollar broke. Local equity is confirming: BVSP -13.8% on the month at z=-2.80, EWZ -16.9% and 14.3% below its 200-day at the 14th percentile.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +0.5% to 5.4623 and +2.1% on the week, +4.6% on the month at z=1.33 and turning up, while DXY -0.6%, EURUSD +0.7% and GBPUSD +0.7%. CEW -0.5% confirms EM FX broadly did not get the dollar memo.
trades.stop: 5.30 — a close below that means the dollar move finally transmits to LatAm and the local stress is resolving.

trades.name: Short homebuilders
trades.line: Short ITB/XHB — mortgage 7.24%, the duration bid just died
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy XHB Jan puts 5% out of the money. Pair against long XLF if you want sector-neutral.
trades.thesis: The homebuilder rally of the past month was pure duration beta on a 33bp drop in 10-year yields, not a housing improvement. The actual rate the customer pays is 7.24% and rising. Strip the bond rally and there is no earnings engine.
trades.trigger: 10-year back up 4bp to 4.95% for a third session and 30-year to 5.32%; the 30-year mortgage is +21bp on the month and +109bp year-to-date at the 89th percentile. On 11/3 the group broke: DHI -5.0%, ITB -3.6%, XHB -2.5%, XHB/SPY -2.8%. Both ITB and XHB are now rolling over and below their 200-days despite a +7.9% and +5.5% month.
trades.stop: 10-year back below 4.70% or the 30-year mortgage back under 7.00% — a genuine rate relief rally would carry this group higher.
trades.target: ITB -10% from 93.52; XHB/SPY back toward the 0.125 area.
